statement: Let (T, B) be an ordinary rational klt pair on a normal compact Kähler space of dimension at most four, globally Q-factorial in the Weil-divisor sense, with canonical sheaf a rational line bundle. Put D = KT + B. Every D-negative extremal ray R ⊂ NA(T) has a projective contraction f : T → Z with connected fibres and normal compact Kähler target, such that f∗ H1,1 BC(Z) = R⊥ , ρ(T/Z) = 1, −D is f-ample. (3.4) Here ρ is the rank of global line-bundle degrees on contracted curves. The target has rational singularities and Rjf∗OT = 0 for j > 0. If dim Z < dim T, this is a Mori fibre space. Otherwise f is bimeromorphic, and precisely one of the following occurs. (i) The exceptional locus is one prime divisor E. Put T′ = Z, B′ = f∗B and D′ = KT′ + B′. Then D = f∗ D′ + eE (e > 0). (3.5) (ii) The contraction is small. For an adjoint Cartier index r > 0, the intrinsic algebra Rr = M m≥0 f∗OT (mrD) (3.6) is locally finitely generated, and T′ = ProjZ Rr is the ordinary flip. It has a small projective morphism f+ : T′ → Z with connected fibres. Put B′ = ϕ∗B and D′ = KT′ + B′, where ϕ : T 99K T′ is the induced small map. For a sufficiently divisible choice of r there is an actual isomorphism OProjZ Rr (1) ≃ OT′ (rD′ ). (3.7) In particular D′ is a rational line bundle and is f+-ample. Passing to a sufficiently divisible Veronese leaves T′ unchanged. In both birational cases, T′ is compact Kähler and globally Weil-divisor Q-factorial, its canonical sheaf is a rational line bundle, and (T′, B′) is klt. Strong global Q-factoriality is preserved when imposed on T. A supplied global canonical Weil divisor is transported to a canonical Weil divisor on T′. No prime divisor is extracted. All log discrepancies weakly increase; the increase is strict for every original prime contracted by the step, and, for a flip, for every place centred in either exceptional locus.
